Macrons

Theme

Money, work & business · Work & responsibility

income noun

also earnings, revenue, returns, rental income

classical

Nep. Att. 14.3: omnisque ejus pecūniae reditus cōnstābat in Ēpīrōticīs et urbānīs possessiōnibus
Plin. Ep. 2.4.3: reditus propter condiciōnem agellōrum nesciō minor an incertior

reditus, reditūs m.

noun, fourth declension

income, returns (of money or land)

Literally a coming back: what money or land brings in. In this sense not in Cicero, but in Nepos, Ovid, Livy and Pliny’s letters (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • vectīgal, vectīgālis n. — income, rents

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Par. 49: ex meō tenuī vectīgālī, from my modest income; Cic. Off. 2.88: vectīgālia urbāna rūsticīs

    Properly a tax paid to the state; Cicero uses it of his own rents and income.

  • frūctus, frūctūs m. — the yield of land or capital; income

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.25 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 11.2.2: frūctus praediōrum (Lewis & Short)

    What a property produces, in kind or in money.

Examples

  • omnisque ejus pecūniae reditus cōnstābat in Ēpīrōticīs et urbānīs possessiōnibus

    and all his income came from his properties in Epirus and in the cityNep. Att. 14.3

  • Ex meō tenuī vectīgālī dētractīs sūmptibus cupiditātis aliquid etiam redundābit.

    From my modest income, once the costs of greed are taken off, there will even be something left over.Cic. Par. 49

See also earn, profit, property, economy.
